# VIGIL

Robot fleet monitoring, remote terminals and guided recovery.

- Dates: 2026
- Status: Lab platform
- Areas: Software engineering; Robotics
- Stack: Python · FastAPI · Paramiko · ROS
- Topics: Python; Robotics; ROS; FastAPI; Operations; Web/API
- Public case study: https://mgiorgetti.com/project_details/project-vigil.html

## Problem

A robotics lab needs a consistent way to observe fleet status, investigate a robot and repeat diagnostic or recovery procedures.

## Contribution

Developed a robot-fleet operations dashboard using FastAPI, Paramiko and ROS interfaces, with browser-based SSH terminals.

## Technical approach and public case study

Monitor robots, open remote terminals, and run saved diagnostic and recovery workflows.

- Full-stack engineering

- FastAPI · Paramiko · ROS

- Internal platform

Online and offline robots, selected for diagnostics from the fleet dashboard.

### Monitor, diagnose, and recover

Monitoring covers connectivity, battery, ROS topics, and runtime activity. Saved workflows make checks and fixes repeatable.

- Observe Background monitors collect robot status and detect changes in connectivity.

- Diagnose Run a saved check or investigate through a live SSH terminal in the browser.

- Recover Execute an ordered fix. Per-robot coordination prevents conflicting jobs from running together.

### Shared execution, robot-specific checks

#### Shared runtime

The backend opens SSH sessions, runs commands, evaluates output, and reports state. WebSocket streaming keeps the browser terminal interactive.

#### Versioned checks and fixes

Versioned JSON definitions describe each robot family’s commands and workflows, keeping platform details out of the execution engine.

**Terminal sessions**

Scoped to a robot and browser page session, including interactive input and terminal resizing.

**Workflow isolation**

Monitoring coordinates with active diagnostics and recovery work.

**Definition validation**

References and command tokens are checked on startup and reload.

## Results and limitations

The case study describes an internal lab platform. It does not publish a reliability benchmark, fleet-wide uptime result or public hosted service.
